text:
maria-chen: quick heads-up — ran an end-to-end perf sweep on staging with both FA2 and FA3 kernels. seeing a ~12% p50 latency regression on short-seq (<=64) workloads when the picker chooses FA3 by default. attaching notes.

alex_g: ugh ok. do you have the profiler flame and the kernel selection logs? can you paste the sampling output?

maria-chen: pasted below. main signal is higher L2 stall time and some memcpy spikes when switching pages for KV cache. differences come up when batch size distribution is skewed to many tiny requests.

jamal: is this the case where batching heuristics flip to bigger micro-batches under FA3 and that trips a fallback path?

maria-chen: maybe. profiler snippet:
```
# pprof summary (short sequences, 128 workers)
FA2: avg p50 18.3ms, p95 40.1ms
FA3: avg p50 20.6ms, p95 44.8ms
hotspots: memcpy_gdr_copy, kv_page_map, fa3_matmul_kernel
```

ryan: that memcpy_gdr_copy smell — sounds like device<->host shuffling. any host staging buffer changes in FA3 path?

maria-chen: FA3 uses a slightly different staging allocator for paged attention; it does opportunistic page pulls which may trigger extra small DMA ops when KV cache regen happens. reproducer command:
```
./run_perf_sweep --model=gpt-medium --seq=32 --dist=batch:many_small --kernel=auto --telemetry=on
```

alex_g: can we try forcing FA3 but with `KV_PAGE_FETCH=lazy` env to disable opportunistic pulls? would like to see delta.

maria-chen: tried that. with `KV_PAGE_FETCH=lazy` p50 drops to 19.0ms — much closer. So eviction/regeneration pattern interacts with FA3 allocator.

jamal: interesting. so two axes: kernel math path + allocator/page policy. Picker currently biases by seq_length and perf profile; it doesn't account for KV page churn. we should add a quick heuristic: if workload has high small-batch fraction + KV churn > X, prefer FA2.

ryan: agree. we can expose flag to runtime: `attn.kernel.priority` with values `latency|throughput|stability`. default remains `latency` but can be overridden per-route. would help Dedicated customers too.

maria-chen: proposed rollout plan (short):
- feature-flag: `ff:attn_kernel_v3` off by default
- canary group A (10% traffic): FA3 enabled + `KV_PAGE_FETCH=lazy`
- canary group B (10% traffic): FA3 enabled + allocator fixes (dev branch)
- metrics to watch: p50, p95, memcopy rate, KV page faults/sec, failed requests
- automated rollback rule: p50 regression > 7% for 5m OR error rate spike > 0.2%

alex_g: add also a `batch:small_frac` telemetry tag so we can route heuristics server-side. i.e., if small_frac>0.6 then prefer FA2.

jamal: agree. implementation tasks:
- runtime: add `kv_churn` metric + tag export (ryan)
- picker: add churn-aware rule and expose override (alex)
- kernel: land allocator patch that reduces opportunistic DMA for small pages (maria + perf team)
- infra: extend canary config in deploy bot (ops)

ops-bot: deploy plan stub created: deploy/attn-v3-canary-5009876543 (status: queued) :gear:

ryan: i'll own the canary config + threshold alarms. can we draft the telemetry query now? something like:
`SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 50) AS p50, percentile(latency_ms,95) AS p95, sum(kv_page_faults) FROM traces WHERE kernel IN ("FA2","FA3") GROUP BY kernel, 5m`

maria-chen: adding a lightweight smoke test for KV churn that simulates many short conversations and forces eviction. test script attached inline:
```
# simulate churn
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -d '{"seq":32, "prompt":"hi"}' >/dev/null &
  sleep 0.01
done
```

alex_g: once allocator patch lands we should also run microbenchmarks for fused attention op — FA3 fusion sometimes produces different register pressure which can increase L2 misses. let's capture `l2_miss_ratio` in perf runs.

jamal: small request: document the FF matrix and safe fallbacks in the runbook. include explicit steps to flip flags per region and the rollback CLI. i can draft the runbook if someone provides the exact env names.

maria-chen: env/flags to include in runbook: `FF_ATTEN_KERNEL_V3`, `KV_PAGE_FETCH`, `ATTN_KERNEL_PRIORITY`. i'll add them to the doc.

ryan: timeline? can we aim for a cautious rollout tomorrow with canary A, then B 24h later if green?

maria-chen: yes. i'll open PR for allocator patch + runtime metric in the morning. leaving a checklist here: 
- [ ] PR: allocator patch
- [ ] PR: picker churn heuristic
- [ ] Telemetry: batch_small_frac + kv_churn tag
- [ ] Canary config + alarms
- [ ] Run smoke churn test post-deploy

alex_g: thanks — ping me on the PR and i'll run microbench suite. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy/attn-v3-canary-5009876543 moved to in_progress by ryan at 5009876570

maria-chen: will post results in this thread once canary completes. if anyone wants to join the monitoring channel set up for the rollout ping me and i'll add you.

ryan: watching. thanks team.
